cluster_stories.title: Anthropic in Talks to Buy AI Startup Decart for $6 Billion
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, in what would be the Claude maker’s largest known acquisition. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic Eyes $6 Billion Decart Deal | Open Interest 8/13/2026
cluster_stories.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and David Gura on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Anthropic eyes its biggest deal yet, with a potential $6 billion Decart acquisition as it moves closer to an IPO. SpaceX clears its first lockup expiry, but bigger swings may be ahead. Plus, producer prices come in softer than expected. And Liftoff CEO Jeremy Bondy joins us on AI-driven ad growth, while Threadneedle's Ann Berry warns investors about the risks hiding in private markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic IPO valuation hinges on $190-200 billion 2028 revenue forecast
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic is projecting 2028 revenue of roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, according to two people familiar ​with the company's financials, a figure that has not previously been reported. The projection dwarfs the $47 billion revenue "run rate," reflecting the firm's current pace of business, that the company publicized as recently as May, and shows the scale of growth investors are being asked to underwrite.
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC IPO: Projecting $200B Revenue by 2028

polls.description: Escalating geopolitical tensions as China launches autonomous AI cyberattacks on Taiwan while the US pressures nations and companies to choose sides in the AI technology war.
polls.question: Should the US force allies to choose sides in AI development?

cluster_stories.title: US to tell partners they must pick sides in AI race with China
cluster_stories.summary: By pressing countries to choose sides the US hopes to starve China of resources in a race to make the most sophisticated AI, which ​could be used for military or economic dominance. In July, Chinese President Xi Jinping launched a rival "World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization", promoting his country's open-weight technology as a challenge to US influence over the fast-moving sector.
cluster_stories.headline: US FORCES ALLIES TO PICK SIDES IN AI RACE WITH CHINA
